metadata.title: Provincial Rental Housing Corporation: names, name treatments and identity

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: Pemco Holdings Ltd. renamed British Columbia Housing Corporation

evidence.locator: OrgBook BC, corporation BC0052129, name history

events.interpretation_notes: In the Legislature on 29 June 1976 the minister, Hugh Curtis, explained that the idle Pemco Holdings had become B.C. Housing Corp., at first to receive federal financing. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: Order in Council 3283/1976 authorizes the Crown’s representative to vote to rename British Columbia Housing Corporation as Provincial Rental Housing Corporation
events.interpretation_notes: The order carries the provincial arms in its standard heading, not a corporate mark. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

evidence.locator: OrgBook BC, corporation BC0052129, name history

events.interpretation_notes: From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: A page of the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing’s 1976 annual report given to the corporation, its name set in three lines of bold serif capitals

evidence.locator: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, annual report 1976, printed page 70 (PDF page 73); Legislative Library of British Columbia

events.interpretation_notes: A name treatment in a government report, with no emblem, monogram or seal; not evidence of a logo. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: The corporation’s name in slanted capitals on a Kootenay District Crown grant map
events.interpretation_notes: Lettering naming the grantee, not a logo or seal. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: “PROVINCIAL RENTAL HOUSING CORPORATION” in widely spaced orange capitals in a narrow ruled box, heading its section of BC Housing’s 2000/01 annual report

evidence.locator: BC Housing annual report 2000/01, printed page 59 (PDF page 61)

events.interpretation_notes: A designed section heading within BC Housing’s report; not shown to be a separate PRHC logo. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: The Riverview Lands (səmiq̓ʷəʔelə) transferred to the corporation
events.interpretation_notes: The site’s sign protocol of 12 May 2022 (page 2) specifies the BC Housing and Kwikwetlem First Nation logos and graphics for its identity, not a separate PRHC mark. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.

events.title: A letter “on behalf of Provincial Rental Housing Corporation”, on BC Housing letterhead with the BC Housing emblem and signed by a BC Housing director, to the District of 100 Mile House

evidence.locator: District of 100 Mile House council agenda, 12 November 2025, PDF page 7

events.interpretation_notes: PRHC has no employees; BC Housing acts as its agent, and its correspondence carries BC Housing’s identity. From research summaries supplied on 2026-11-12, which cite this source; it was not re-read in this pass unless the locator says so.
